depiction

/duh-PIK-shun/ — stress on PIK · noun

What It Means

A depiction is a picture or other representation that shows someone or something.

The mural's depiction of the harbor includes every boat by name.

Example

The historical novel's rich depiction of life during the Civil War included authentic details about clothing, food, rationing, and the daily struggles of ordinary people.

Depiction is precise here because it means a full representation — the novel shows us both the big picture and small details, both visual and descriptive. Words like 'story' or 'account' are narrower; depiction captures the full scope of representation.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

illustration: An illustration is a single drawing made to explain or decorate a text. A depiction is broader: it can use pictures, words, or both, and it aims to show the whole subject. An illustration serves the page it sits on; a depiction can fill a novel or a mural.

portrayal: A portrayal represents a person or character, and it stresses personality — how someone thinks, feels, and acts. A depiction can take any subject at all, from a harbor to a whole war, and it stresses the fullness of what is shown rather than the character inside it.

account: An account tells in words what happened — a report of events, given plainly and in order. A depiction goes further than telling: it shows its subject, building a detailed picture in images or scenes, not just a record of facts.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

omission: leaving something out of the account entirely

concealment: deliberately hiding something from view

Where it sits · how fully the subject is presented — mention → sketch → description → depiction

mention vs. depiction: A mention is far weaker than a depiction: a mention names something in passing, while a depiction actually shows or represents it in detail.

sketch vs. depiction: A sketch is fuller than a mention but still far below a depiction: a sketch gives only the rough outlines of its subject, while a depiction works out the whole picture.

description vs. depiction: A description is fuller than a mention but plainer than a depiction: a description lists details in words, while a depiction builds a complete picture of its subject.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: down, completely (Latin)

Root — pict (from pingere, pictus)

Root — pict (from pingere, pictus): to paint (Latin)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or process of (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: De- ('completely') + pict ('paint') + -ion ('act or process of') builds 'the act of painting something out completely' — a depiction is a picture, description, or other representation of someone or something.

Use the root in a new word: picture

Use the root in a new word: picture: The artist's picture of the harbor hung in the hall — picture and depiction both come from Latin pictus, 'painted.'

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Use depiction when you want to emphasize the full act of showing or representing something — especially when both visual and written elements matter. For a purely written account, 'description' is simpler. For just pictures, say 'illustration.' Depiction is the broader, more artistic choice.
